core_obligations: Split W_infinity = T union E with E the inverse image of Z, and check that the local construction applies to Q|_E because (Q|_E)|_{T cap E} is zero or of rank less than p in degree 0 by assumption (A2) (proof lines 10234-10242).
Define c'_p(Q) = (E -> Z)_* o c'_p(Q|_E) o C and note that it is a bivariant class by proper pushforward (proof lines 10243-10247).

Verify the identity (Z -> X)_* o c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{X x 0}) by the displayed chain of six equalities, using that E -> Z -> X equals E -> W_infinity -> W -> X, the comparison of c'_p(Q|_E) with c_p(Q|_{W_infinity}), bivariance of c_p(Q) with respect to i_{infinity,*}, the defining property of C, another bivariance step, and the identification of W_0 with X; the same chain gives the statement for P'_p(Q) (proof lines 10248-10272).
proof_roadmap: Set up E and T, and apply the local construction to Q|_E (proof lines 10234-10242).
Assemble the bivariant class from the local class, the proper pushforward and the Gysin-at-infinity class (proof lines 10243-10247).
Verify the pushforward identity by the six-step chain of equalities (proof lines 10248-10272).
difficulty_reason: Under assumptions (A0) that the Chern classes of the perfect object Q on W are defined, (A1) that b : W -> P^1_X is an isomorphism over A^1_X, and (A2) that there is a closed subscheme T of W_infinity containing all points over X setminus Z where Q restricts to zero or to a finite locally free module of rank less than p in degree 0, the lemma constructs canonical bivariant classes P'_p(Q) and c'_p(Q) in A^p(Z -> X) satisfying (Z -> X)_* o c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{X x 0}) (statement lines 10203-10231). The proof splits W_infinity as T union E with E the preimage of Z, forms the class C of the Gysin-at-infinity lemma and the class c'_p(Q|_E) of the local construction lemma, defines c'_p(Q) = (E -> Z)_* o c'_p(Q|_E) o C, and then verifies the required identity by a chain of six equalities in the bivariant Chow groups, each justified by a named input: the equality of the composites E -> Z -> X and E -> W_infinity -> W -> X, the comparison of c'_p(Q|_E) with c_p(Q|_{W_infinity}), the commutation of the bivariant class c_p(Q) with i_{infinity,*}, the defining property of C, and finally the identification of W_0 with X (proof lines 10234-10272). Assumption (A2) is exactly what makes the local construction applicable to Q|_E, and assembling the three classes consistently is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
